messages:
Alex Kim: FYI we saw a persistent queue build in us-west last night for ~40m, 95th token latency spiked ~2.5x. Not full OOM, but PGPU util stayed high and KV cache churned. Thinking we should pick a consistent short-term admission pattern — curious opinions on prefer-queue (short hold) vs soft-degrade vs immediate reject.
Priya Nair: Can you paste the timeline / signal we used? was it memory pressure or just qlen?
Alex Kim: primary signal was queue_length and tail latency. mem pressure was transient on a few nodes. infra-bot posted the alert: `ALERT us-west:queue_len>120 for >10m, 95th_latency>600ms`
Sam Ortiz: Short take: if mem is fine, prefer short holds (queue) up to X ms, then degrade. Immediate rejects are easier for tail safety but ruin client UX.
Jenna Li: Our existing runbook has threshold pairs but they're fuzzy. I propose a micro-runbook: - hold up to 300ms if queue_len<200 and node_mem_pct<85 - soft-degrade (lower model size / quantized variant) between 300-1500ms - reject beyond 1500ms or mem>92%
Priya Nair: That looks sensible. Need to define what soft-degrade is concretely: fallback to `open-1.3q` + prefix-cache lookup? Also who owns rollout?
Sam Ortiz: Soft-degrade = route to quantized variant + enable prefix-kv hit reuse + reduce max_tokens by 20%. Example config snippet we can canary: ```json
{
  "admission_strategy": "tiered",
  "hold_ms": 300,
  "soft_degrade": {
    "model": "open-1.3q",
    "token_limit_pct": 0.8
  },
  "hard_reject_after_ms": 1500
}
```
Alex Kim: nice. Two concerns: 1) This increases cost on fallback model if traffic shifts. 2) Routing churn when lots of requests hit degrade path. Need circuit-breaker counters and a short cool-down on switching.
Jenna Li: Agree re churn. Add per-node degrade_rate limit (e.g., 10rps degrade cap) and a cooldown window of 60s after a degrade spike. Also emit `degrade_ratio` metrics per model/route.
Priya Nair: Operational checklist for rollout: 1) add metrics (degrade_ratio, hold_count, reject_count) 2) implement feature-flagged config in canary cluster (us-west-2-prim) 3) run 2-hour synthetic traffic ramp to validate 4) review cost delta 5) gradual ramp to 10%/50%/100%.
Sam Ortiz: I'll own the canary and the synthetic job (+alert if degrade_ratio>5% or cost_delta>10%).
Alex Kim: I'll update the runbook doc and add the decision table. Jenna, can you add the per-node rate limit and cooldown?
Jenna Li: Yep. I put a quick implementation PR draft in the repo, will link once ready. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident summary: 2165-05-06T03:12Z — root cause noisy batch spilling traffic to inference cluster; mitigation applied: manual scaling + emergency warmpool spin-up; post-incident: 2.3% p95 SLA breach for US-WEST.
Priya Nair: One more behavioral question — if queue increases but mem steady, do we prefer longer holds to preserve accuracy? or degrade sooner to save tails? We should codify per-customer tier.
Alex Kim: Good point — map tiers: "plat" -> allow longer hold (500ms), "standard" -> default 300ms, "free" -> 100ms then degrade. Add to rollout checklist.
Sam Ortiz: Also add test cases in load harness: spike+gradual recovery, sustained noisy tails, mem-blip scenario.
Jenna Li: I will draft the playbook section with decision table and sample config variants. Expect PR by EOD.
Alex Kim: OK assigning owners: Sam = canary + load tests, Jenna = code+playbook, Priya = metrics+runbook review, Alex = runbook doc and rollout coordinator. We'll aim for a staged rollout next Tue.
Priya Nair: Sounds good. If we hit unexpected churn during canary, fallback plan is immediate rollback to current policy and scale up warmpool.
Sam Ortiz: noted. I'll post canary status in #eng-oncall while running.
Alex Kim: Thanks all. Short summary pinned: implement tiered admission with hold->soft-degrade->reject thresholds, per-node degrade caps, canary + metrics + cost guardrails.
Priya Nair: :wave:
